title: Living on the fat of the land. Their butteries and larders. I’d like to see them do the black fast Yom Kippur.
html_source: Consumption comes up again this time in reference to rich, sumptuous foods. This seems to have moral implications too. Bloom is criticizing Catholics for having such large families who consume much rich foods such as butter, lard, fat all products of Ireland’s cattle raising activities. He doubts their ability to be able to abstain from this consumption, talking of the fast which Jew’s undergo once a year on Yom Kippur. The ability to be able to abstain from consumption, Bloom appears to suggest, might be equated with some sort of superiority.
